title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that Congress must refuse to provide any additional funds or exceptional regulatory support to companies or financial institutions facing insolvency or financial collapse due to exposures to acute stress within the artificial intelligence market and must provide support to all harmed Americans instead.
action: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House of Representatives says Congress should refuse to give extra funding or special regulatory aid to companies or financial institutions that are at risk of collapse due to acute stress in the artificial‑intelligence market. Instead, Congress must focus on providing support to all Americans who are harmed.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 is designed to set national standards for AI research to ensure systems are trustworthy and dependable. It establishes oversight, transparency, safety testing, and accountability measures to protect the public while encouraging responsible innovation.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to disclose when and how artificial intelligence is used in its services so veterans and staff can understand AI’s role. It also sets standards for documenting AI decision processes, conducting audits, and protecting patient data to ensure accountability and privacy.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act seeks to ensure that artificial intelligence tools used in processing veterans’ benefits claims operate transparently, fairly, and with proper oversight. It establishes standards for data use, auditability, and accountability to protect veterans from bias and errors in automated decision‑making.

title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The act is designed to protect elections from harmful AI‑generated misinformation, such as fake videos and news that could mislead voters. It sets rules for detecting, reporting, and countering AI‑based disinformation so elections stay fair and trustworthy.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act aims to safeguard users from misleading AI-generated content by mandating clear labeling and disclosure of AI involvement. It also sets penalties for companies that deceive consumers through undisclosed or false AI outputs, ensuring higher transparency and accountability in AI deployment.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act seeks to improve the safety and protection of advanced artificial intelligence systems by setting strict security standards for their creation and use. It likely requires developers and organizations to perform detailed risk analyses, implement robust safeguards, and report any security incidents to help prevent harmful or malicious exploitation.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act establishes a dedicated task force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to develop and coordinate national policies for protecting AI systems. It seeks to create standards, guidelines, and collaborative efforts among federal agencies, industry, and academia to identify, mitigate, and reduce risks and vulnerabilities in AI technologies.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Act establishes a framework for identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks that artificial intelligence systems may pose. It requires companies to implement security safeguards, conduct regular risk reviews, and report potential threats to a federal oversight body.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 establishes a framework for overseeing and coordinating AI-driven physical systems such as autonomous vehicles, drones, and industrial robots. It requires manufacturers, operators, and regulators to set safety standards, share data, and maintain accountability so these systems can work together safely and transparently.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act is intended to shield the integrity of elections from the spread of misleading or manipulative content generated by artificial intelligence. It would establish rules to detect, flag, and hold accountable any AI systems or platforms that produce or facilitate such deceptive election-related content.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act requires that artificial intelligence systems which can modify their own code or behavior be closely observed and regulated to prevent unintended or harmful outcomes. It establishes oversight mechanisms to keep such systems safe, transparent, and aligned with human values.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act aims to prevent the development and deployment of autonomous systems that could act independently in ways that pose risks to safety or privacy. It proposes strict oversight, clear accountability standards, and penalties for companies that fail to comply with safety and transparency requirements.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary pause on building or operating new AI data centers. This pause is intended to give lawmakers time to evaluate the environmental, energy, and equity impacts of large AI computing facilities before they expand further.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 establishes a federal board to investigate cybersecurity incidents that involve artificial intelligence. The act aims to strengthen national security and protect the public by ensuring thorough investigations into AI-driven cyber threats.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: Make AI Work for Americans Act seeks to guide the development and deployment of AI systems so that they directly benefit the U.S. public by promoting transparency, accountability, and equitable access to emerging technologies. The act also establishes oversight frameworks and incentives to encourage responsible innovation that safeguards consumer interests and supports economic growth.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act is expected to set legal guidelines for how artificial intelligence systems are developed, monitored, and reported within China. It likely requires organizations to disclose AI capabilities, usage metrics, and compliance with national security and ethical standards, aiming to strengthen oversight and transparency.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 is a proposed law that requires all medical diagnosis and treatment to be performed by licensed doctors rather than by automated AI systems. It aims to protect patients by ensuring that human medical professionals remain the sole decision‑makers in healthcare.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: Congress is proposing to create the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats, which will be part of the Executive Office of the President. The office will focus on identifying and addressing potential threats posed by AI and emerging technologies, and will likely have additional responsibilities as outlined in the bill.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence creates a new committee to oversee and guide AI-related policy, research, and regulation. It defines the committee’s purpose, membership, powers, and responsibilities for shaping the nation's AI strategy.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 proposes a framework for assessing the potential risks of AI systems before they are deployed. It aims to protect public safety by requiring comprehensive risk assessments and mitigation plans for AI technologies.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed U.S. law aimed at regulating artificial intelligence, setting standards for safety, accountability, and transparency. It seeks to balance innovation with protections for consumers, businesses, and society at large.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 establishes rules to reduce the environmental footprint of AI systems, focusing on energy consumption, data center efficiency, and lifecycle emissions. It requires companies to report environmental metrics and offers incentives for adopting greener AI technologies.
